Petitioner Smt.Alamkonda Manjula @
 A.Manjula D/o A.Giddareddy  W/o C.Vivekananda Reddy,
 Aged 27 years,
 Residing at No.2/359,
 Thirumalanagar,
 Adoni, Andra Pradesh-518 301.

 3rd Cross, Murugeshpalya,
 Bengaluru-560 017.

 V/s  Respondent Bengaluru Metropolitan  Transport Corporation (BMTC)
 2 SCCH-18 MVC 670/2022  Rept by its Managing Director,

 Bengaluru-560 027.

JUDGMENT Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
1
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.
The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:

2. That, on 01-11-2021 at about 7.30 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Scooter bearing registration No.KA-05/JP-8052, which was ridden by her husband, on Service road of MKK Road, from eastern side towards western side,
when they crossed major portion near Kuvempu statue junction at Sampige road, at that time driver of BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F-9013 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed from southern side towards northern side and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to K.C.General Hospital, Bengaluru for first aid, then she was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as an inpatient and undergone surgeries and she had spent about Rs.10,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and she was a housewife.
After the accident, she could not do any work due to her severe injuries.

As her service to the family has to be treated in terms of income, hence, petitioner has suffered loss of income due to accidental injuries.
5.
It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F- 9013.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver of said vehicle by the jurisdictional Malleshwaram Police in Crime No.78/2021.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notice, the respondent has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement of the respondent has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

Further it has admitted that the bus BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F- 9013 belongs to this respondent and denied the manner of accident, age,
avocation and income of the petitioner.
Further contended that false case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is defence of the respondent that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
It is also contention of the respondent that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exhorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
2 8.

On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, she had sustained grievous injuries in an motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 01.11.2021 at about 7.30 a.m. on Sampige road, near Kuvempu Statue, within the jurisdiction of Malleshwaram police station, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F-9013 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? and from whom?
3) What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she herself examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
Apart from this, placed the evidence of Senior Associate Medical Records, Manipal Hospital as PW2 and got marked Ex.P12 to Ex.P16.
In addition to this placed the evidence of Dr.S.Ramachandra, as PW3 and got marked Ex.P17 and Ex.P18.
Further placed the evidence of Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao as PW4 and got marked Ex.P19 to Ex.P23.
10. On the other hand, the driver of the respondent corporation got examined as RW1 and not got marked any document on his behalf.

11. Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.
12.

My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F-9013, the alleged accident had taken place,
consequently she had sustained grievous injuries.

14. On the other hand, it is the strong contention of the respondent that, he was the driver of the BMTC bus, and on his scheduled trip from KR Market to Lakshmipura and was proceeding Lower bridge at Malleshwaram Circle, at that time rider of the two wheeler bearing No.KA-05-JP-8052 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed agaisnt the bus.
Hence, the rider of the two wheeler is responsible for cause of accident.
Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
3
15. On the basis of the rival contentions of both the parties, it is necessary to rely the evidence placed on record by both the parties.
16. The petitioner in order to prove her case, examined herself as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to P7
. Ex. P1
-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.78/2021 of Malleshwaram Traffic Police Station.
Ex. P2
-true copy of the first information statement given by one Vivekananda Reddy Ex
. P3- true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4-spot sketch, Ex.P5-IMV report,
Ex.P6-wound certificate, Ex.P7-true copy of charge sheet in Crime No.78/2021 of Malleshwaram Police.
17. In order to substantiate the defence of the respondent, has examined its driver as RW1.
RW1 has reiterated the defence made in the written statement.

18. At the time of cross-examination of PW1, though several questions put to the witness, but nothing has been culled out from her mouth to believe all the defenses of the respondent forthcoming in the written statement.
Even at the time of cross-examination of RW1, though he has stated that false case has been registered against him.
But not placed any documents on record to prove the same.
The respondent herein, except making allegations against the petitioner, no supportive and reliable documents placed for consideration to believe his defenses against the case of the petitioner.
19. In the light of the discussions held above, I hold that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-05-JP-8052.
Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory materials on record, to prove the aforesaid issue.

Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative ISSUE NO.2 :
20.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

21. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as Alamkonda Manjula Alias. A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation. "

Pain and Sufferings;
22.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Multiple abrasions over the feet and right elbow 2) Head injury with a) fracture left occipital bone b) fracture of left parietal bone, fracture brass of wing of sphenoid c) Displaced fracture left quaditory card d) diffuse cerebral edema
e) multiple contusions right temporal and frontal lobes 3) Blunt injury to the chest and abdomen 4) Fracture of left leg tibia/fibula distal leg 23.
In connection with the above said injuries, the doctor is of the opinion that the injury No.1 & 3 are simple in nature and the injury No.2 (a) to (e) and 4 are grievous in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hospital marked at Ex.P9, it reveals that petitioner took the treatment as ain inpatient from 1.11.2021 to 21.11.2021 and 30.11.2021 to 4.12.2021.
Apart from her evidence placed the evidence of Senior Associate Medical Records marked at PW2.
He has placed authorisation letter, inpatient records, MLC and x-rays at Ex.P12 to Ex.P16.
In addition to their evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.S.Ramachandra as PW3.
PW3 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner had sustained traumatic brain injury, fracture tibia and fibula left leg distally.
Further placed the evidence of Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics as PW4.
He has deposed in his evidence that at the time of admission she was drowsy and agitated, opening eyes to pain, localising to pain and uttering inappropriate words.
She had a GCS Score of 10/15.
CT brain revealed right fronto temporal multiple contusions, axial hemorrhages and diffuse cerebral edema.
He has palced OPD record, skull x-ray report, audiometric report, neuropsychological assessment report and mini mental statement examination report at Ex.P19 to Ex.P23.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, she could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment as an in patient as well as an outpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
5

Loss of income during treatment period:
24.
PW1 has stated that, she was a house wife.
In such a situation notational income is apt to be taken applying the same principle like other cases.
Since a woman cannot work by looking the clock, as her work is 24 hours work and whole day she is working for the sake of the welfare of her family members.
On going through the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9, which discloses that the petitioner took the treatment as ain inpatient from 1.11.2021 to 21.11.2021 and 30.11.2021 to 4.12.2021.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to her to do daily routine work and to do her work for livelihood at least for a period of four months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by her.

Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.60,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medial Expeneses;
25.

The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.1,33,189/- as per Ex.P10, Ex.P11 for Rs.88,755/- less discount of Rs.6,592/-, it comes to Rs.82,163/- (Rs.55,726/- paid by the company) remaining Rs.26,437/- paid by the petitioner in toto Rs.1,59,626/-.
No other contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,59,626/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
26.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely she could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
27.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, she had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by her as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, she had sustained grievous injuries.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.Ramachandra examined as PW3.

PW3 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained traumatic brain injury, fracture of tibia and fibula left leg distally for which the petitioner underwent right fronto tempero parietal decompressive craniectomy, evacuation of sub-dural and temporal contusion done on 4.11.2021, percutaneous tracheostomy, closed reduction and internal fixation of left tibial and distal fibula K-wiring done and Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
6 discharged on 21.11.2021.
28.

PW3 further stated that petitioner again admitted to the hospital on 30.11.2021 and diagnosed post decompression craniectomy she underwent bone flap replacement on 1.12.2021 and tracheostomy closure on 2.12.2021 and again admitted to Mazumdar Shaw Medical centre on 30.10.2021 and diagnosed left tibia implant in situ for which she underwent left tibia implant removal and was discharged on 31.10.2021.
29.
On the basis of entire evaluation of the disability of the petitioner, PW3 had opined that, total physical disability of the petitioner is 28.42% of left lower limb and 14.21% of whole body.

In support of his evidence produced clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P17 & Ex.P18.
30.
At the time of cross-examination of PW3, admitted that he is not treated the petitioner.
Based on the documents he has assessed the physical disability.

This witness also denied the suggestion that,
he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.
31.

PW4 -Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padamashree Diagnostics,
deposed that he was evaluated the petitioner on 13.7.2024, 16.7.2024 and 3.8.2024 for the purpose of assessing her disability.

Further stated that at the time of admission to Manipal hospital,
petitioner was drowsy and agitated, she was opening eyes to pain, localising to pain and uttering in appropriate words.

CT brain revealed right fronto temporal multiple contusions extra axial hemorrhages and diffuse cereb ral edema, the petitioner was admitted to ICU and treated, she had a cardiac arrest and was revived.
She underwent right fronto temporo parietal decompressive craniectomy, evacuation of sub-dural hematoma and temporal contusions.
She was on mechAnical ventilator.
She underwent tracheostomy on 9.11.2021.
At the time of discharge, she was opening eyes, moving limbs, she was on tracheostomy tube, rt feeds and foley'x catheter.
Further petitioner underwent cranioplasty and tracheostomy closure.
CT brain during follow-up revealed right frontal and temporal gliotic changes with thin extra axial collection.
Further assessed the disability, she has a MRS score of 1, this amounts to disability of around 10%, this disability is pertaining tow hole body.
32. At the time of cross-examination of PW4 denied the suggestion that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner in higher side.
33. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW3 & PW4 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW3 & PW4 seems little bit exorbitant.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3 & PW4 it is just and proper to consider disability 20% instead of 14.21% & 10%
The same will meets the ends of justice.
34. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, her age was 27 years.

In support of the age proof,
she has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8 for consideration.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 6.8.1993.
The accident occurred on 1.11.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 28 Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
7 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '17' is to be taken into consideration.
35. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in her evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident, she was a house wife.
Since a woman cannot work by looking the clock, as her work is 24 hours work and whole day she is working for the sake of the welfare of her family members.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2021.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/- for the year 2021.

36. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of her future, in a slight manner, to do her daily routine work, as well as to do her work for livelihood on going through her age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 17 X20/100= Rs.6,12,000/-.
Loss of amenities;
37.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to walk, she cannot bend, unable to walk long distance and lift weight.

On perusal of evidence of PW3 and PW4 also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as her work for livelihood as an agriculturist.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future medication:
38.
In connection with the future medication, PW3 & PW4 have not stated about the future medication.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

39. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.Pain and Suffering Rs.1,00,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 60,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3. Medical expenses Rs.1,59,626-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 30,000-00 and Conveyance Charges Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

A. Manjula vs B.M.T.C on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156239594/
8
5. Loss of future income Rs.6,12,000-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 50,000-00 7.
Future medication NIL Total Rs.10,11,626-00 40.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,11,626/- (Rupees ten lakh eleven thousand six hundred and twenty six only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
41.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F-9013, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
As such, it is the strong assertion of the petitioner that, the respondent being the owner as well as internal insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, the respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
42.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/ s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,11,626/- (Rupees ten lakh eleven thousand six hundred and twenty six only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Alamkonda Manjula Alias.

9 Draw award accordingly.
